exposure: Lower Uterine Segment (LUS) thickness measured via transvaginal ultrasound (TVS)
outcome: Cesarean Delivery (CD) due to labor dystocia
cohort: The study included 130 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies at 34-36+6 weeks of gestation.
finding: LUS thickness measurement alone has limited predictive capacity for cesarean delivery due to labor dystocia in singleton pregnancies.
mod_finding: The mean LUS thickness did not differ significantly between vaginal deliveries (6.69 mm) and cesarean deliveries (7.01 mm), indicating limited predictive value for mode of birth.
